WinAppMigrator turns an app installed on one Windows PC into a single installer you can run on another, even when the app's own installer is long gone.

Pick the app from this PC, from a drive pulled out of a dead or dying machine, from a `.vhd` or `.vhdx` image of one, or from an old Windows 7 or later PC over your network. WinAppMigrator works out everything that belongs to it, its files, registry entries, services, drivers, scheduled tasks, shortcuts, and the runtimes it needs, with its user data and license if you choose, and shows you what will go in before it builds anything. The installer it makes shows what it will set up before it changes anything, checks every file by SHA-256, puts back what it changed if anything fails, and can be undone later from Settings.

## Download

- **`WinAppMigrator-v{{VERSION}}.exe`**: the app. One file, with nothing to install, for Windows 10 and 11, x64.
- **`WinAppMigrator-v{{VERSION}}-windows-x64.zip`**: the same app, with the README, the changelog, and the licenses.

[Getting started](https://randynorthrup.github.io/WinAppMigrator/Getting-Started) says how to use it.
